Air Quality — Monitoring and Control

AFSCME air-district technicians, LIUNA environmental laborers, IUOE and USW plant crews

EPA Method 9 visible emissions (40 CFR 60 Appendix A), EPA 40 CFR Part 58 ambient air quality monitoring, the Bay Area Air Quality Management District's own regulations, and a site's Air Monitoring Plan under a cleanup order

The air a neighbourhood breathes is measured by a short chain of people and instruments, from a fence-line monitor to a stack test to a certified eye reading a plume, each one held to a different standard for a different reason. This block runs that chain end to end, from where the readings are taken to where the emissions actually come from.

Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

What it proves

Competency: Measure, read and report what a stack and a fence line are emitting

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 3 of its 6 stations, against EPA Method 9 Visual determination of the opacity of emissions (40 CFR 60 Appendix A); EPA 40 CFR 58 Ambient air quality surveillance.

These stations also count toward:

  • Confined Space entry, attendance and atmosphere (1 of this track's stations count toward it)

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: EPA Method 9 visible emissions (40 CFR 60 Appendix A), EPA 40 CFR Part 58 ambient air quality monitoring, the Bay Area Air Quality Management District's own regulations, and a site's Air Monitoring Plan under a cleanup order. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
